classification.difficultyReason: Two journeys on one grid. Students read arrival times, find an intersection that falls on Kai's stationary section, find a gap at one time, and calculate a speed from graph readings. Each step is direct but there are several representation links.

content.prompt:
The graph shows the journeys of two riders, Kai and Tess.
Both ride from home to the lake along the same road.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Who reached the lake first, and by how long?

answer.worked: Tess reaches the lake at 12:00 and Kai reaches it at 13:00. Tess arrived $1\text{ h}$ sooner.
The journey lines meet at 10:30, so Tess passed Kai at 10:30.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How far apart were they at 11:00?

answer.worked:
At 11:00, Tess is 32 km and Kai is 24 km from home.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Distance apart}&=(32-24)\text{ km}\\&=8\text{ km}\end{aligned}$$

Tess rode 48 km from 09:00 to 12:00, which took 3 h.
$$\begin{aligned}s&=\frac{d}{t}\\&=\frac{48}{3}\\&=16\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$$
